sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch. In dense regular connective tissue 'fibers are parallel to each other, enhancing tensile strength'; 'Ligaments and tendons are made of dense regular connective tissue'; in dense irregular tissue 'the direction of fibers is random', and 'The dermis of the skin is an example'; elastic tissue gives arterial walls strength and the ability to recover their shape after stretching.

brief.situation: You are the student assistant for the histology practical at Whitmore Community College (fictional). The digital slide catalog is the exam's answer key. Two students report that slide 14, labeled 'tendon (dense regular)', does not look like their notes. Slide 15 is labeled 'dermis (dense irregular)'. The exam opens at 10:00. It is 09:05.
handover: Both slides were rescanned last week and re-uploaded.

Each step takes working minutes, and the clock moves by the minutes it takes. The deadline runs on the same clock.
Shipping is final for this case. Afterwards you record what you found and explain your reasoning.

scoring.modelReasoning: Students who say the tendon slide looks wrong are right if its fibers run in every direction. Tendons and ligaments are dense regular connective tissue, with parallel collagen fibers that resist pull in one direction; dermis is dense irregular, with fibers in all directions. Slide 14 shows random fibers and slide 15 parallel ones, and the upload log shows the images attached in reverse. Reattach the images to the right slides; swapping labels breaks the printed question numbers, and dropping the slides removes required tissues.
